tasks.title: Lecture #48
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.
tasks.transcript:
Man: For decades, archaeologists believed that complex societies and the monumental architecture, the large buildings signifying them, only emerged after agriculture, and that farming was essential for societal development.
After all, before agriculture developed, people tended not to settle in a single place, but moved from place to place in search of food. We call such people nomadic hunter gatherers. They were continuously on the move to hunt and collect food. And for people who aren't settled, it was more practical to live in small mobile groups rather than in complex societies. Or so it was believed.
But the excavation of the ancient site of Gobekli Tepe through a wrench in this whole story. Gobekli Tepe, dating back about 11,000 years, consists of multiple massive pillars arranged in circles and is considered the world's oldest known temple. Remarkably, it predates the earliest evidence of agriculture in the area by several thousand years.
This suggests spiritual practices, not agriculture, may have caused early communities to form. Many scholars interpret the site as a ceremonial center, a periodic gathering place for nomadic hunter gatherers. More recently, archaeologists there did find traces of things like food processing areas, stone tools for grinding grains, as well as actual plant residues. Yet these residues come from local wild grains, not domesticated crops, and the structures may not indicate year round habitation. So while Gobekli Tepe might have hosted temporary gatherings, the evidence still supports the idea that spiritual practices played a central role in early societal development.

questions.stem: What traditional view did the excavations at Göbekli Tepe challenge?

options.A: That early humans were mostly plants
options.B: That monumental architecture began in Göbekli Tepe
options.C: That agriculture was necessary for complex societies
options.D: That early humans were mostly nomadic

questions.analysis: 答案: C 题目问的是: 哥贝克力石阵的发掘挑战了哪种传统观点？ 定位原文: "For decades, archaeologists believed that complex societies and the monumental architecture... only emerged after agriculture... But the excavation of the ancient site of Gobekli Tepe threw a wrench in this whole story... Remarkably, it predates the earliest evidence of agriculture in the area by several thousand years." 选项分析: A. That early humans were mostly plants (早期人类主要是素食主义者) - 错误。文中未提及。 B. That monumental architecture began in Göbekli Tepe (纪念性建筑始于哥贝克力石阵) -错误。虽然它是已知最古老的，但挑战的核心在于它与农业的时间关系，而非它是否是第一个。 C. That agriculture was necessary for complex societies (农业是复杂社会形成的必要条件)- 正确。传统观点认为先有农业才有复杂社会（纪念性建筑），但哥贝克力石阵在没有农业的情况下就出现了复杂建筑，直接挑战了这一观点。 D. That early humans were mostly nomadic (早期人类主要是游牧的) - 错误。讲座承认早期人类是游牧的，挑战的是游牧人类无法形成复杂社会/建筑这一推论。

questions.stem: What does the speaker point out about nomadic people?

options.A: Information about them is preserved in the form of spoken stories.
options.B: Their numbers increased about 11,000 years ago.
options.C: It was difficult for them to find enough food during certain seasons.
options.D: It was practical for them to move in small groups.

questions.analysis: 答案： D 题目问的是: 关于游牧民族，说话者指出了什么？ 定位原文: "We call such people nomadic hunter gatherers... And for people who aren't settled, it was more practical to live in small mobile groups rather than in complex societies." 选项分析: A. Information about them is preserved in the form of spoken stories. (关于他们的信息以口头故事的形式保存下来。) - 错误。文中未提及。 B. Their numbers increased about 11,000 years ago. (他们的数量在大约 11,000 年前增加了。) - 错误。文中未提及数量变化。 C. It was difficult for them to find enough food during certain seasons. (在某些季节他们很难找到足够的食物。) - 错误。虽然这可能是事实，但不是说话者在此处强调的重点。 D. It was practical for them to move in small groups. (以小群体形式移动对他们来说是务实的。) - 正确。文中明确提到“it was more practical to live in small mobile groups”。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the plant remains found at Göbekli Tepe?

options.A: They are strong evidence of people living at the site year-round.
options.B: They suggest that people at the site fed their animals there.
options.C: They suggest that very large amounts of grains were stored at the site.
options.D: They came from wild species that grew in the area.

questions.analysis: 答案： D 题目问的是: 关于在哥贝克力石阵发现的植物遗存，说话者说了什么？ 定位原文: "Yet these residues come from local wild grains, not domesticated crops..." 选项分析: A. They are strong evidence of people living at the site year-round. (它们是人们在遗址全年居住的确凿证据。) - 错误。文中明确说“structures may not indicate year round habitation”。 B. They suggest that people at the site fed their animals there. (它们表明人们在那里喂养动物。) - 错误。文中未提及喂养动物。 C. They suggest that very large amounts of grains were stored at the site. (它们表明遗址储存了大量的谷物。) - 错误。文中未提及大量储存。 D. They came from wild species that grew in the area. (它们来自当地生长的野生物种。) -正确。文中明确指出是“local wild grains, not domesticated crops”。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what do scholars still consider likely about Göbekli Tepe’s function?

options.A: It was a ceremonial site for nomadic groups.
options.C: It was a trading hub for thousands of years.
options.D: It was a permanent farming settlement.

questions.analysis: 答案： A 题目问的是: 根据说话者，学者们仍然认为哥贝克力石阵的功能可能是什么？ 定位原文: "Many scholars interpret the site as a ceremonial center, a periodic gathering place for nomadic hunter gatherers... the evidence still supports the idea that spiritual practices played a central role..." 选项分析: A. It was a ceremonial site for nomadic groups. (它是游牧群体的仪式场所。) - 正确。文中多次提到“ceremonial center”和“spiritual practices”。 B. It was a military outpost. (它是一个军事前哨。) - 错误。文中未提及。 C. It was a trading hub for thousands of years. (它是数千年的贸易中心。) - 错误。文中未提及贸易。 D. It was a permanent farming settlement. (它是一个永久的农业定居点。) - 错误。文中明确指出它早于农业，且可能是“periodic gathering”（周期性聚会），而非永久定居。
